title: The Maltese Falcon

scenes.visual_description: A gritty 1920s private investigator's office in San Francisco. A yellow oak desk dominates the foreground, covered in a green blotter and dusted with grey cigarette ash. A brass tray overflows with butts. Buff-colored curtains hang at a window revealing a building court. Harsh afternoon light filters through smoke-hazed air. The room features a swivel chair and an oaken armchair. Palette of tobacco browns, dingy yellows, and dull greens.

A 1920s San Francisco bedroom at night, shadowed and gritty. A bed with green and white checked linens sits disheveled. A bedside table holds a telephone, a pouch of Bull Durham tobacco, and a tinny alarm clock. A single white bowl light hangs on gilded chains from the ceiling. The atmosphere is smoky and masculine, with tobacco browns and harsh electric light cutting the gloom.

A steep, fog-choked San Francisco street corner at night. A large billboard frames a gap between buildings leading to a dark, sloping alley. Wet pavement glistens under distant streetlamps. An ambulance is parked near the alley mouth. Flashlight beams cut through the thick mist, illuminating rough wooden fences and damp earth. A moody noir atmosphere with deep shadows, cold greys, and muted blues.

scenes.visual_description: The grand lobby of a 1920s San Francisco hotel. Tall purplish marble columns rise to a gilded ceiling, casting long shadows. In the foreground, a polished mahogany reception desk with brass fittings stands ready. To the side, a quiet alcove contains a flat-topped writing desk. The atmosphere is hushed and formal, lit by electric chandeliers that reflect off the marble floors. Cool tones of violet, mahogany, and brass.

A chaotic 1920s hotel apartment living room in cream and red tones. A walnut settee and a brocaded oval-backed chair sit facing each other in the foreground. Open trunks and scattered clothing suggest a hasty, unfinished arrival. Soft morning light filters through the windows, illuminating the disarray. The atmosphere is intimate but unsettled.
